utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. The registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, can I just very briefly raise one very small matter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: That's the order of witnesses. I want to let the Defence know. I mentioned to you earlier this week, I mean to the Chamber earlier this week, the order, and I think I said that Muhamed Bicic would be called, then Hasan Bicic, then Ibrahim Salkic. They're all witnesses that give general evidence but also concern the defendant Milan Simic in particular. The order will have to be changed, and I now propose to call Hasan Bicic first, followed by Muhamed and then Ibrahim. So I thought I'd let the Defence know that. That's been occasioned by the fact that Muhamed Bicic has got this American court commitment, and they're arranging some sort of videolink for him to testify in the American case from here, in fact, and so that means he's going to be -- have his mind occupied with that and attending to that. So for that reason I've altered the order, and I just want the Defence to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may have the floor for just one short comment. Only two days ago, I have asked the Prosecutor, because I knew that the session in the American court is scheduled for the 22nd of October. I asked them loud and clearly whether Muhamed Bicic will be here or not and whether Muhamed Bicic will be the first witness. They said Muhamed Bicic will be the first witness. On the eve of the witness coming into the court, we have been notified that there is another change. This is the fourth time they've changed it from Muhamed to Hasan. I mean, with all due respect, I really believe this is -- I mean, this is really not something that should be happen before this Tribunal. The order of this Honourable Trial Chamber was that we have a week in advance programme how the witnesses are coming so we can prepare ourselves for the cross-examination, and, therefore, in this case, we really are brought into the position where we have prepared everything for Muhamed Bicic, then Muhamed Bicic is exchanged for another witness. And this might go on forever with that. Because we cannot really prepare within one day. Okay. In this particular case, we have a whole week -- a whole weekend so that we can prepare, but I mean as a matter of principle, I believe this is not acceptable. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It is the experience of the Tribunal that there arises incidents which make it impossible for the Prosecutor to stick to their order of calling witnesses. What the Trial Chambers in the past have done is that at least within the week the same witnesses are called regardless of the order, and we have always accepted the changes in practice because of various problems. Now, in this case, as you rightly pointed out, it would be ideal to have the order retained as was first agreed upon, but there is an intervening incident and then the witness has to come later on, more or less later on but within the same week, hopefully. But at least you have the weekend, as you said, to prepare for this one alteration. And the Tribunal does expect counsel to work on Saturdays and Sundays during the trial proceedings so that we go ahead with our trials. That is understood, and we do -- you wanted to say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Of course we understand, and we agree a hundred per cent with you, Your Honour. The point is that -- the point I was trying to make was that only 48 hours ago, I insisted whether it's going to be Muhammed Bicic, because I know that he is committed to go into the American court, and I have told my learned colleagues that. And they said, "No problem. He's not going over there." And that is the point which I am trying to make, because we were brought into the position that we know for sure that it's Muhammed Bicic on this week and the beginning of next week, whatever commitments he has. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. di Fazio, you understand that he had insisted whether or not you were sure, because according to him, he was sure that this witness would be giving testimony in the other case. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Well, I appreciate that and I understand my learned friend's concerns about that. I'm not suggesting that he should not be concerned about that, and I apologise for any inconvenience caused to him. But there are intervening causes that have necessitated this change, and it's not the sort of matter that can't be rectified by the Defence. After all, both witnesses give fairly brief statements. In comparison, for instance, to the statements of Mr. Izetbegovic or Mr. Dragan Lukic or Mr. Sulejman Tihic, they are positively minuscule. It's a question of -- I can't even --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That is understood that there was an intervening problem -- MR. DI FAZIO: Eleven pages of statement, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- but as much as possible, let's stick to the order. MR. DI FAZIO: I'll endeavour to do that, but the problem arose because of the late development of this videolink conference idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. MR. DI FAZIO: And it would mean, probably, having to stop Muhammed's evidence, Muhammed Bicic's evidence, halfway through so he can go off and attend to this other court commitment, and that would be undesirable from his point of view and from the Chamber's point of view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Notwithstanding that we all know the primacy of the Tribunal. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go ahead. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go ahead. MR. DI FAZIO: -- making any comment about that. And I take on board what Mr. Zecevic has said, and every effort will be made to stick to the order that's announced --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- whenever and wherever possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we continue with our cross-examination of the witness, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Izetbegovic. After analysing your testimony so far, I have come to the conclusion, Mr. Izetbegovic, that I have to remind you of a number of facts. The first fact is that before the International Criminal Tribunal -- that you are before this Tribunal. The second fact is that you have taken a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. And a third fact is one that my learned friends from the Prosecution may not have informed you of, as well as the Witness and Victims Unit, that it is possible to institute criminal proceedings against a witness in this Tribunal for perjury. Yesterday I was very correct when I asked you about a particular fact and gave you the opportunity to correct yourself, when I asked you whether you were a hundred per cent sure about a certain fact. I will continue to be correct, and I shall give you another chance. We agreed yesterday that there were unintentional lies due to -- MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I object to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- memory faults or something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I object to this. I don't recall any agreement about unintentional lies yesterday, and if the question is to be asked, a question by Mr. Pantelic is to be asked, let him ask a question, not make a speech. Let's get to it and let's ask the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, I was about to ask Mr. Pantelic why he finds it necessary, as counsel, to start warning the witness, because that's the duty of the Trial Chamber, Mr. Pantelic. You are given permission to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And I hope you will stick to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You are way out of your obligations under the Rules of the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I hope so, because you will be ordered out of this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam President, for your directions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And the co-counsel will take over and the trial will continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know there is a lot of possibilities, but let's go to the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Izetbegovic, on the 16th of October, on page 2360 of the transcript, lines 16 to 20, said the following. I will read it in English, as I don't have a transcript in your language: [In English] "I saw on the coffin the surname Zurovac." This is a moment that I want to clarify this name. Who is Zurovac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume he is Zarko Zurovac's son, who was technical director in Mehanika.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Izetbegovic, do you know Zarko Zurovac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know the name of his son?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've forgotten that. When he was little, we moved away. We were no longer neighbours. He grew up in the meantime. I know his mother's name, Vasa, and I know his sisters too, but we didn't meet each other for a long time after that. It is the only Zurovac family that lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The witness said -- intervention for the transcript, for the interpretation. The witness said the only Zurovac family that live in Orasje, O-r-a-s-j-e?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I knew, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You lived close by. In fact, you were next-door neighbours, were you not? That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not next door. Orasje's a small place, so even a hundred metres can be considered a neighbouring house. But we did socialise. We visited each other at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So you lived in Orasje, not in Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A long time ago. In 1966 until 1968.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And you celebrated when Zarko Zurovac's son was born, whose name you don't know. You celebrated his birth?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. He had two little girls. I can't remember exactly whether it was the birth of one of the girls - it was a long time ago - but I know that we did celebrate the birth of one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because on the 16th of October, you said that you remembered the event. So do you remember or do you not remember?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which event?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The same event, Madam President. I'm referring to his statement from page 2360, line 16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I just want to know, is it the event surrounding the birth or the death?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, of the birth, of the birth of son of this neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 16th of October, you said you remembered the event. Now you're telling us that you don't remember. So please make up your mind so that we can move on.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you a long time ago that -- not to hold me to the dates. I said I attended some celebrations. I don't know how it's gone down. How could I have said that I knew exactly when he was born, on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Izetbegovic, you do not seem to understand me. When I'm saying the 16th of October, 2001, I'm relying on the transcript of your testimony here. I'm not saying that he was born then. So let me remind you. You said then, and that is on the 16th of October, here before this Trial Chamber: [In English] "As we were neighbours, next-door neighbours, we celebrated when he was born. I remember that." [Interpretation] I'm asking you now, do you remember when his son was born and the fact that you celebrated the event or do you not remember? I'm not asking you for the date.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I celebrated many events. I remember that I celebrated the birth of two children with him. I can't remember exactly which one now. So if it is so important which birth it was and when he was born, I moved out, so I didn't know the boy well after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but we are now talking about the event when you entered the military helicopter at Pelagicevo. And bearing in mind everything that you said, that you knew his father and that you were family friends, do you still abide by what you said earlier, and that is that the surname Zurovac was written on the coffin and that it was the coffin of the son of your friend whose name was Zarko Zurovac? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was written -- the word "Zurovac" was written on the coffin. I cannot claim I remember the first name. But it did say "Zurovac" 100 per cent, and I assumed it was the son of Zarko Zurovac, because I didn't know any other Zurovac family in Orasje, and I know there weren't any other Zurovac families there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In your testimony on the 16th of October before this Trial Chamber, you said the following [in English] inter alia --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He's speaking about this person in the coffin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, how important is this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very important, Madam President, because I want to establish whether we hear the truth here or not truth. So then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The witness has explained that he saw a coffin with the name "Zurovac." He remembers that. He has said that so many times. He assumed that the person in the coffin must be the son of Zurovac, because according to him, he knew the Zurovac family in Orasje and it was the only family then. So what is the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The problem is, Madam President, that he said something which I just want to read on 16th of October, and I want to clarify that thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I hope it is an important issue to your defence, because what is important here is that there was a coffin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. And also what is important for Defence, Madam President, is whether we have reliable witnesses here or not, or whether we have the truth or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I know you have to deal with credibility, but this is not the way to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I just want to finish this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I hope you're finishing this particular point --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- because it doesn't carry any importance at all. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honour pleases, I understand when Mr. Pantelic started this line of questioning about the coffin what he was trying to achieve, and with all due respect, he has achieved that. This witness has said now twice that he's 100 per cent sure of the identity of the person who was in the coffin, and we can contrast that with other evidence that we have heard and we can all draw our own conclusions. It's like trying to draw blood out of a stone. You can't get any better than 100 per cent certainty by this witness. The point's made, isn't it?.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And usually it's important to remember that you have your closing arguments --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- and you can deal on the contradictions if you see they are contradictions. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. There is some other contradiction and I just want to clarify that. So if you permit me, Madam President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in your statement of the 16th of October, you said, among other things, the following - I will read it in English - and this relates to the son of Zarko Zurovac, who was allegedly inside this coffin. You said he [Previous translation continues]... So that means you saw his face. How did you know how he was dressed? Was the coffin open? Did it have a glass cover or what? How could you establish that he was dressed? Please answer that for me and then we can move on.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said any such thing. The coffin was closed and carried inside, and I don't know who could have written any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. So we've cleared that up. It must be an error in the interpretation, which is quite possible, and we've cleared that up. But I would like to know who could have added any such thing.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not retarded to have said anything like that. The coffin was closed. So how could I say that he was dressed? There's no logic there. So I think something is being planted there for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I was just reading the official transcript of these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can get that correction through the audio unit. I hope this time it will be done so that we get a written transcript as corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let us go back, Mr. Izetbegovic, but really, to be efficient, please say yes or no in answer to my questions regarding this event that we were discussing yesterday. The Prosecutor seemed to indicate that there were some false death sentences which were threatening you, and this is something that the President of this Chamber accepted, so this is a very serious issue, and that is why I wish to clear it up. My first question, Mr. Izetbegovic, is: In your statement to the investigators in 1994 and 1995, you said the following: "On one occasion the death sentence was read out for Tihic and myself. The guard brought in a newspaper, Vecernje Novosti, a Belgrade newspaper. Tihic read out that we had been sentenced to death and that we had been sentenced to death by our own party as traitors." Something to that effect was stated by Mr. Tihic, too, in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Please be brief in your questions, because by the time you come to the end of your statement, I forget what you were going to say. I have a feeling that you are trying to mislead me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I cannot shorten your own statement. It is my duty to read it out in extenso. My question now is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you can read it slowly, especially slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I just did it. I just did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, Mr. Izetbegovic: This statement that you gave to the investigator, do you agree with it? Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you please read it out once again which was this statement and ask me to comment on it alone, and then move forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: With your permission, maybe it would be better that I can give this -- his own statement. Maybe he can read it. Maybe it's better for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry? In Serbo-Croat, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In Serbo-Croat?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Just indicate the paragraph to the usher. Then he can indicate it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I already made the line here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So please read that, Mr. Izetbegovic, slowly, and tell us whether you confirm what you said or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And the witness should read it aloud so that we have it on record, since --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: You want the witness to read it out loud?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In Serbo-Croat. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Into the microphone, you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps the usher could -- perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I thought the microphone was on. MR. DI FAZIO: It is. He's intent on reading it. Perhaps if Mr. Pantelic could ask him to re-read it out loud.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, will you please read out aloud, because the Court and the Prosecutor think that would be a good idea. Read out the highlighted lines.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it's been read out already. It's been read out once, the death sentence for Tihic and me. "The guard brought a newspaper, the Vecernje Novosti, a Belgrade newspaper. Tihic read out that we had been sentenced to death and that we had been sentenced to death by our own party as traitors."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If you don't mind, read out the next sentence, too.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it hasn't been underlined.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Never mind.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "One of the guards asked why I didn't react, and I answered that I had never heard of a political party condemning people to death."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why didn't you underline it? "Later on, in Sarajevo, I found a newspaper in which it was said that I had actually been executed, that the death sentence had been carried out." I don't know what's unclear there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Everything is clear to me too. So you still abide by what you said then?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We now have to clear up something that you said before this Court on the 16th of October, because there are some things that are not clear, and this is partially reflected on the understanding of the Trial Chamber of that particular fact. You said in this Court that on the basis of certain evidence and proof, which might have been false, and because of the procedure from Samac and at Batajnica, were sentenced [as interpreted] to death by the Yugoslav authorities, and that then Tihic read out that sentence to you at Batajnica. I think, on the basis of all these facts, that in fact it was in the Belgrade papers that the news item was published and printed that you had been sentenced to death by your party in Sarajevo, and that that was read out to you, the newspaper article, and not an official sentencing act of any kind. Could you clarify that for me, please?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you for being so persistent. I shall try and answer. Mr. Attorney, I think that you will recall, and I think I remember very well, that I said that I didn't see an act of any kind, that it was read out from the newspapers, and that there was a document, but that I did not see it; I did not have it in my hands. Perhaps Mr. Tihic will be able to answer that better when you see him here, because I didn't have the actual act or document in my hands. I saw that he was just holding a piece of paper in his hand. He wasn't near me for me to see, nor did I dare ask to see the piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that. Thank you for your answer. So what the Prosecutor asked you re: the 16th of October is, to all intents and purposes, incorrect, and the answer you gave him is not correct. I am speaking about the fact that -- actually, what I mean is that the Prosecutor probably misunderstood the whole episode, which led him to ask you the questions he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. You can't make that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Just go ahead with your questions. You are dealing with the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- not the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And stick to your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, sorry, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, may I just interpose with a clarification from the witness. Mr. Izetbegovic, can you clarify how many times were you told, were you told, that you were sentenced to death? Was it once or twice? And where was this done: in a park or in an office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At Batajnica, in a cell, in the cell we were sitting in. We were told once, and that was not repeated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: And was Tihic there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Tihic was reading it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Your Honours, in spite of your instructions and directions, the Defence were not provided by the, actually, sort of official transcript, so I have to read from my draft version, and the pages are not corresponding to the regular pages. So that's a problem. It's a rough version.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tihic [sic], the Prosecutor asked you on the 16th of October: [In English] "On this occasion when you were lined up and told that the death sentence has been passed upon you, were you informed for what it was for? In other words, was there some connection between the imposition of this death sentence and overthrowing the system or whatever that you had been informed about in Bosanski Samac?" [Interpretation] That is what the Prosecutor asked you, and this is your answer. Listen to me carefully, please: "It was mostly based on everything from Bosanski Samac, and they kept talking about the undermining and overthrowing of the system and the failure to report for the mobilisation of the army, that he hadn't responded to the call-up. Then I was seen as a deserter and I said, 'Well, it is no longer my army. It was once, but it is no longer my army. It is a different country altogether, a different state altogether.' That was my defend [sic]. I defended myself in that way." [Interpretation] You see, Mr. Izetbegovic, you make no mention of a newspaper article here at all or that somebody had fabricated your death sentence from Sarajevo. You are building up your case in direct response to the Prosecutor's question, that on the basis of certain facts from Samac and from Belgrade, you were sentenced to death, and that is what this Trial Chamber understood, that it was a sort of psychological duress. And I'm taking you back to your statements of 1994 and 1995 and I'm reminding you of Tihic's statement. And I state - and this is my thesis, and please put me right if I'm wrong - that Tihic read out something from some newspaper, or explained this to you, and that it was a newspaper article and not an official sentencing document. Am I right or am I not? Please answer so we can move on.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said it all. Do I have to repeat ad infinitum, until I go mad? I think it should be clear to you by now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Would you please answer my question, Mr. Izetbegovic, and the question is the following: Did you on that occasion have knowledge of the fact that your party in Sarajevo brought a death sentence of any kind against you and Tihic and that that was read out to you by Tihic? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned - and we're still in Batajnica. Let's stay in Batajnica. You mentioned in your statement that -- you referred to a certain General Tumanov in a situation in which you were having problems with the investigations and the proceedings against you, and you asked them to call General Tumanov. You wanted to see General Tumanov. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I asked to see him, because they didn't believe anything I was saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Let's pause. Can you explain to me briefly your relationship with General Tumanov?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it is my duty to give you information of that kind. I don't think I need do so, especially as I don't think this is the subject we are dealing with in this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: First of all intervention for the transcript. It's T-U-M-A-N-O-V instead of "O", Tumanov.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You mean the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. The name of this General.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Izetbegovic. I'm not quite certain that we do not have the right to learn of the nature of your relationship with the general. We have several ways open to us. If you have anything confidential, we can move into a private or closed session, but at all events, we do have the right to learn about everything -- learn everything about something that is mentioned in the proceedings and if it has any bearing on this trial. So I'm asking you once again, and I should like you to answer me briefly, what is your relationship with General Tumanov? You said that you didn't wish to answer that question, but I'm asking you to do so now.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as you were so nice about it, let me try. The nature of our relationship or how we came to know each other was through business, the business that we did with each other with respect to the exchange of Vukovar citizens, nothing else. That's how we came to know each other, on the basis of that exchange. We had lunch together. We talked during lunch. He left a very good impression on me. I thought he was a fine man, and I thought that in that difficult period for me that it would -- he come in handy. And as you know, somebody drowning catches at straws.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that situation fully. Tell me, please. How many times did you meet with General Tumanov approximately?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, where is that going to take us? I mean, where are you going from there? Please go on to the ingredients of the charge and the elements which your client is facing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will follow that direction. It is only one question. I want to establish the nature of this relation and then to make some checking on the field, because this name was appear for the first time in these proceedings, not in his previous statement. So probably because it's related to the process of exchanges on the territory of Bosanski Samac in 1991 and as well as 1992 to some extent, we don't know yet, I just want to establish some facts, because this is opportunity for this witness to tell us. Just the last question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Tumanov is which branch of the armed forces, the infantry, the navy, or the air force? Tell me that and we can move on.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't able to notice that on the uniform that he wore. It wasn't marked, except for his rank, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, in your statement, the one you gave to the Prosecutor, when you spoke about certain political activities in Samac, you said that you relatively frequently had contacts with the other parties, the SDS party and the HDZ, in order to transcend the problems and to try and find a peaceful solution to events in 1992. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You said that about a week prior to the attack, the SDS organised a meeting in the municipality. Now, if the attack was on the 17th, this would mean that it might have been around the 10th of April, that meeting in the municipality. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I keep saying that I don't remember dates. I'm very bad with dates. That is one of my faults. I remember dates very poorly, even telephone numbers. But approximately, taken broadly and as there was no time to hold a second meeting, I can conclude that it might have been around about that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, I understand your situation. These are criminal proceedings. Places, dates, descriptions are very important matters, and that is the crux of my cross-examination. But if you say you don't remember, well and fine. That's another matter. And bearing the mind the fact that your memory was fresher in 1994 and 1995 and that you said, "Approximately one week prior to the attack I was at a meeting convened by the SDS and chaired by Blagoje Simic." Do you still stand by that time category? Was it at that period? And that's why I'm trying to refresh your memory, as indeed my learned friend of the Prosecution did before me, because you're now talking several years after -- you were talking several years after the event.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but so -- I needed a lot of time to become stable, to stabilise myself. I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us yesterday that with members of your own party and with members of other parties, you followed the efforts of the International Community diligently with respect to solving the problems in Bosnia. That's true, is it not?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You also told us that certain topics linked to delineation in Bosnia, demarcation on an ethnic basis, and certain constitutional solutions at that time were the overriding topic elsewhere and in Samac as well by the same token. Is that -- would that be correct to say?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I think that a lot of things began in Samac as well. I do not exclude the HDZ when I say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, in your statement, you said that you were present in the municipality, going about your business, and you were the vice-president of the executive board at the time, and that you came to the meeting where the representatives of other municipalities and parties were present; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Excuse me, counsel. When you say "in your statement," do you mean the statement that he gave to the Prosecutors?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: His testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, his testimony. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It would be easier to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I have to make reference, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: When you refer to the statement here in the Court, just refer to it as the transcript. I think that will differentiate it from the other statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Counsel can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry, Your Honours. Just for your reference, it was quite extensive way of -- line of questioning, so it's between page 2221 and 2248. So this is a part of this particular meeting that was called.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, Mr. Izetbegovic, nobody called you to attend the meeting; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I received no invitation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You were the vice-president of the executive board of the municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, Mr. Lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You were the vice-president of the SDA party in Bosanski Samac; correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And on that day - we don't know when because of your memory - came to the municipal hall where you encountered the representatives of various parties from the surrounding areas and various political leaders of the different parties; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. And there were military structures as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On the occasion, you said -- that is to say, in your testimony before this Trial Chamber, you said that they were the representatives of Odzak; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I enumerated some of the ones I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let's just move forward. Answer my questions. Odzak; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Orasje, Gradacac, Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Those were the presidents of the municipalities, because you said that by hierarchy they were automatically the presidents of their parties as well.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume so, yes. The mayors or presidents of the municipal assembly were there. I knew them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Among other things, you said that your party president was not -- did not attend.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he was present. I don't remember exactly. He tended to steer clear of meetings, political meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. You say that on page 228 -- 2228, lines 14 and 15, that he was not present. Mr. Izetbegovic, would you agree with me that in fact the topic of the meeting was one of the activities, inter-party activities in the region in order to discuss certain solutions of the International Community about the peaceful solutions to the situation in Bosnia and the different divisions therein? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We did not have any --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No. Just a moment. No. That will do. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: The witness must be permitted to finish his answer, and this is a very important area of evidence, as we know. So I don't see that it's fair on the witness for his answer to be -- to be cut off. The witness started -- started to say, "We did not have any" and then was just cut off by Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I see. I see the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But, Madam President, that was, you know, occasion for the examination-in-chief. I mean, this is cross-examination. If you want to mix, you know, principles from examination-in-chief --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. Mr. Pantelic, don't waste time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let the witness complete his answer, and he's going to complete the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said an attempt to divide up Bosnia. Now, why are you constantly leading me to the terrain of the entire republic? I have said umpteen times here that I am talking only about the events in Bosanski Samac itself, and that is the only subject that I am qualified to talk about. So very often in your questions you tend to lead in some state qualities, and I don't want to enter into the realm of the state. So please don't do that. It wouldn't be fair towards me. I consider that I have been fair and said everything I know so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Witness, witness --

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps not everything --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Stick to answers. You and counsel are not to lecture each other. Stick to the answers, give your answer as correctly as you can, and if you have to add that, "I'm limiting my answer to Bosanski Samac," say so. All right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you very much. That is clear, and I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Therefore, Mr. Izetbegovic, we cannot avoid or sidestep the influence of the International Community on Samac and the region, can we? I ask you to take a look at the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, please, would you assist us? It is the map linked to the -- showing the municipalities of Bosanski Samac, Odzak, Gradacac, and Orasje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... exhibit number, unless it's a new map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I don't want to tender it in evidence. This is just for the purposes of identification about the general geographic area. It's a map from the Prosecutor, actually, witness expert who should appear here, just in order to clarify some things. I don't want to tender that in evidence, not yet, I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We can't use the maps which are already an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, because this is a very good map with the good lines of the borders of Dayton Peace Accord, so just to facilitate the explanation of this particular witness. That was my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted to be clear whether we can have it as your exhibit, because you are using it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's not necessary. It's just illustration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I think counsel is referring to a map from the report of Ewa Tabeau, who is proposed to be called as an expert witness in this case. If that is so, then I have no objection to that map being shown to the witness and then marked for identification. The report will subsequently be produced into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, we can proceed along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Just to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The map is from the report of the witness who is yet to come, and it will be produced by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please. You can put it on the ELMO, if you would be so kind, and then ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Izetbegovic, please take the pointer. If you prefer to look at the map directly, please do so, whichever you prefer. Do you prefer to look at the screen or the document itself?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, please, we would like to have a map by itself. Can you zoom it, but -- we have the larger -- the whole map, please. Okay. Thank you. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Izetbegovic, what do you prefer: to look at the screen or the map itself?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in you pointing to the red line. You're a person who understands maps. You were involved in construction and town planning. Show us the top and the bottom red line, which we will agree, I think, is the dividing line on the basis of the Dayton agreements.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This red line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So those are the dividing lines on the basis of Dayton?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. This is the first time I see this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. On the left-hand side, please point out the municipality of Odzak.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please point to Bosanski Samac, the municipality of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Orasje, please.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Modrica.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And Gradacac.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So the witness pointed out the areas asked, as shown on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Izetbegovic. Could you please tell me now: Do you have any knowledge that Odzak municipality was divided according to Dayton?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I learnt from the newspapers, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So your answer is yes, you do know that it was divided. Will you tell us aloud, please, not just nodding.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's the wrong conclusion, because the witness has said what he learnt from the newspapers. It's important to differentiate that, what we learn from newspapers and what is a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. He made a nodding by his head, Your Honour, and therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because it's possible to mislead him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then I just tried to clarify this thing, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- it is not on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. Once he answers according to the way he understands, you leave it there. You don't make a conclusion. You are the same people -- I think the Defence raised that motion, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Izetbegovic, you probably know from the media or from some other source that the municipality of Bosanski Samac has also been divided according to Dayton, if we look at this map.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also from the press.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I see. From the press. But the press can sometimes be a good source of information. Was the Orasje municipality also divided according to Dayton?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose everything was based on Dayton. I don't know. I don't know much about these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was the municipality of Gradacac also divided according to Dayton?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why we're talking at length about Dayton. I can't discuss it. I had no functions, I had no involvement. Please let me free of Dayton.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Izetbegovic. I just wish to see how much you know about what was happening in Bosnia, in your country. You're an educated man. Nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but you have no right to exploit that. That is my private affair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And in addition to that, we stick to the indictment, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I know it's very tempting to go into other matters, but we have a trial here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. This is very much related to the issue that I just raised, I mean the meeting in the municipality, obviously, because of the dividing of the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, this map is self-explanatory. You have got in the legend to the Dayton line, and I don't see your need to ask this witness questions on the division of these areas. It's self-explanatory.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, you're right. But still, this witness is trying to - I don't know for which reason - to avoid direct answers, you know, because this is obviously a fact of common knowledge. So it was just that I might try to establish some facts with regard to the events in 1992 and with the actual situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Izetbegovic, do you remember, since your party president did not attend the meeting, could you mention some other names and personalities who were present when you were discussing the division of these municipalities?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that once - you can look it up in the transcript - and I abide by what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Actually, the problem is that, according to my information, your president, Mr. Sulejman Tihic, did attend that meeting, and it's very strange that you don't know that your president was there if you yourself were there. So that is what I wish to learn from you.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would probably have been sitting together, but as I was alone, then he certainly wasn't there. He may have come later and sat in a corner somewhere, but I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Izetbegovic, for that answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: How much more time? We've had more than one and a half hours yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Ten minutes. Yes. As I said, Madam President, it wasn't my fault. I mean, if the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. How many more minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- yes or no, we would -- otherwise it's a story and story again. Not more than ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, let us now address some aspects of your personality, because it is important for us to establish your credibility. You left your place as president of the party to Mr. Tihic. We're talking about the year 1992.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't leave it to him. We had an assembly meeting, there were elections, and he was elected. I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You have a high opinion of Mr. Tihic. He was a former judge, a former prosecutor, former lawyer. He was a respectable member of your community, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do have a high opinion of him, and he held high positions at the same time as Mr. Zaric and Mr. Pisarevic. They held three key positions, and that is common knowledge: state security, the police, the courts, the public prosecutor's office. You know how important those places are. They held those positions. I'm not sure whether that was at the same time, but all three of them held these high positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please be kind enough, Mr. Izetbegovic. Let us follow the instructions of this Trial Chamber. If you keep elaborating your answers - I'm not asking you that - we will spend the rest of the day here, so please let us follow the instructions we have been given. When I'm asking you a specific, concrete question, please give me a concrete answer. So you have a great deal of faith in the personal and professional qualities of Mr. Tihic. You consider his assessments to be realistic and founded on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think we're going too far.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- an analytical approach.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We are going too far, because Mr. Tihic is a witness in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It is a very important issue here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. I don't think that's the way to go about it. Just ask the question you want to ask. For the reason that he is a witness in this trial, it is important to limit how far you put the integrity of this witness to another witness, regardless of the fact that they were in the same political party or they lived in the same area where the events are being discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's very much connected, Your Honour. Just be patient, just a few seconds, and you will see the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm very patient, Mr. Pantelic, otherwise I would have ordered you out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, you believe that what Mr. Sulejman Tihic says - and he was in the meantime elected president of the SDA party for the whole of Bosnia - carries weight when he says something or writes something. He has prestige; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is impossible to compare those days and the present.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So in those days, you wouldn't say of him that he was reliable when he says something and when he analyses something. We are talking about those days, 1992.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will not discuss anybody's moral integrity, and not his either.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask you that, Mr. Izetbegovic. Let me ask you the following: You like to socialise, you like to go out to restaurants, you like to have fun, don't you?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and sometimes I have a drink too many.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's fine. The fact that you get drunk occasionally absolutely does not affect your regular obligations and your daily life; you're not dependent on alcohol?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never was addicted, and particularly not today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But from some sources, Mr. Tihic believes that you and Alija Fitozovic were prone to alcohol consumption in 1992, and he had problems with you in party activities; is that correct or not? MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, that's an objectional question, for several reasons. It's, A, irrelevant; and B, it's asking this witness to comment on what Mr. Tihic thinks. Now, why doesn't Mr. Pantelic simply ask Mr. Tihic that if it's somehow relevant? So for that reason, I object to the question and the answer. And indeed, there have been a number of questions of this witness asking him, Mr. Izetbegovic, what Tihic thinks of him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I've already given instructions to Mr. Pantelic. He seems to be thinking that he can go around this issue another way. MR. DI FAZIO: I haven't objected thus far, thinking that we'll get to something that I can grasp, but we're not getting there, and so I must object to any further questions that ask this witness what Tihic thinks of him. The person to ask that is Tihic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The objection is sustained. I think the problem appears to be to differentiate how to deal with credibility issues regarding any of the witnesses. I think that is a problem. Do give the questions to the witness dealing with himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I did say do not ask him to discuss the characters of other Prosecution witnesses, especially for Tihic, who is yet to come for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. That was not my intention, Your Honour. It was just a previous question to establish the sort of standards between the -- I mean, within one group of persons, whether they respect each other or not, you know, and then to see what the weight of certain opinions might arise. But I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You see, that's the very danger. This is a criminal trial. It's not a political meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It's even not a meeting in the cafe or bar, I mean, although Mr. Izetbegovic was very extensive about these explanations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You have five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will agree with me, Mr. Izetbegovic, in saying that your party in Bosanski Samac invested a lot of effort to arm members of your party for the purpose of self-protection; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will agree with me, Mr. Izetbegovic, that together with Alija Fitozovic, you were involved in illegal activities of arming? You brought in large quantities of explosives from Croatia. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me, Mr. Izetbegovic, that within your party you had a Reconnaissance Attachment, a Hunters Detachment, a Sabotage Detachment, and a detachment for obstacles and surveyance; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me, Mr. Izetbegovic, that your activities with Alija Fitozovic were directly coordinated with representatives of the Croatian side in Slavonski Brod on Croatian territory?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I would now like to clarify a few things about your property in Samac. The Prosecutor tried to create a situation as if you were having certain problems to regain your property over there. In the first place, Mr. Izetbegovic, you are a co-owner of a house in Bosanski Samac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The largest owner of the house I am living in. There are two more sisters and children of two brothers. Most of it has been carried over to me. Mr. Pisarevic drew up the testament, so he knows best.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I just want to clarify a few things, that's all. You are not the 100 per cent owner of that house. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you want to say that I made a false statement, don't put it to me like that. Such questions can't be answered with a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You're using the same language, so you have forgotten that the interpreters are waiting to interpret.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, it is not my intention to accuse you of falsely testifying, I just want to clarify a point, please. Are you the owner or a co-owner of that house?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are unfair blows. I've told you I have the majority share of that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But that is still your property. That property has been entered as your property in the real estate books; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After my father's death, I am not sure whether we have regulated those things in the books, in the cadastre.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you have every right to do what you will with that property, to sell it or to rent it out or to do what you will; is that right? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is what it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The gist of my question, Mr. Izetbegovic, is that there were no restrictions placed on the part of the authorities in Bosanski Samac with respect to your property, no ban on selling it or any -- any restrictions whatsoever regarding your right to fully control that property. That's all that I wish to establish here.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I have still not filed any request, so I still am not certain as to what I wish to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Izetbegovic. One more point and that will be it. So we can agree, I think, that the houses and property of all the inhabitants of Samac, regardless of ethnicity, Serbs, you mentioned Dusan Simic, your teacher Sofia, and others, of course, were shelled by the Croatian part and in the conflict and that virtually all houses were damaged regardless of the ethnicity of their owners. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say who did the shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but they were damaged during the war operations?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during the war operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But let's clarify that answer. According to you, Witness, that was not done by the Croatian authorities, the shelling, the destruction of the houses. Is that part of your answer or you don't know who did the shelling, who destroyed the houses, all you know is that the houses were destroyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The houses were destroyed. Whose shell fell on them, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. One more question. In connection with the circumstances in the surroundings of Samac in March and April 1992, Mr. Izetbegovic, are you familiar with certain criminal acts committed by Croatian forces against the Serb population in the villages of Sijekovac and the village of Lijesce left of Samac? Do you have any knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. That is the end of my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Re-examination by the Prosecution. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, just on these last few questions and answers, you referred to houses being destroyed and damaged. Was your house destroyed or damaged?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As two shells fell on it from the garden side, the staircase caved in. How it was destroyed, I don't know. So to this day it is not possible to climb upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: But the building is still there, is still standing? It may have received damage?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The building still stands.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, very briefly, very briefly indeed, I'd like to go back to this question of coffins. On the flight in the helicopter from Bijeljina -- sorry, from Pelagicevo to Batajnica, you've told us about a coffin you saw and the name on the coffin. Was that the only coffin in the helicopter?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. You've also given evidence of a flight that you took in a helicopter from Batajnica to Pale. Were there any coffins in that helicopter?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there weren't any.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. On Wednesday the 17th, you were being asked questions by Mr. Pisarevic, and he put to you or suggested that there was a plan of attack, a plan of attack on Bosanski Samac which was made up or devised by the command of an armed unit of the SDA together with the Croatian Defence Council of Bosanski Samac municipality, and you said that you didn't know of any such plan. If such a plan had in fact existed, would you normally have been made aware of it?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably I would have known because I was in the board of the party. So surely I would have known. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness just be given the series of exhibits that were produced by Mr. Pisarevic, D2/4, D3/4, D4/4, D5/4, D6/4, and I'll just deal with them briefly in sequence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: First of all, D2/4. Did you have that document?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: It has at the top, at least in the English translation, a reference to "annex number 2," "copy number 2." What does "annex" mean there?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is probably the document I saw before.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: The system of writing "annex" and "copy" at the top right-hand of a page, was that some sort of system that the SDA --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. di Fazio, I'm sure -- MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry, I didn't see counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The one on the screen is in English and the accused may not follow. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry. I do apologise. Perhaps the B/C/S version could be placed on the ELMO. That's again English. Yes. There we go. And could we just lower it a bit, Mr. Usher, so that we can see the top right-hand corner as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: It's a very quick, brief question. You see at the top right-hand corner there are the words "annex number 2" and "copy number" with a "2" handwritten in. Is that system of identification of documents that the SDA used at the time, back in 1992?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under no circumstances, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Also, the document on the face of it lists the president and the members of the municipality Crisis Staff. Is that an exhaustive list of the members of this Crisis Staff? In other words, were there other people also on the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were people attached. This was the backbone. There were others who participated in discussions when we had them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. When you look at the document itself, D2/4, the B/C/S version, is there any way that you can tell if that document existed by itself or was part of another larger document? In other words, is that page taken from a larger document or did it exist by itself or can't you say?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with the larger document, so I don't know anything more about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now look at D3/4, please. MR. DI FAZIO: Could we have the B/C/S version placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have an objection to the transcript. The witness said, "I am not familiar with the larger document, so I don't know anything more about that." "I think it was on its own," it is not entered into the transcript. Perhaps the Prosecutor could correct that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You mean the complete answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We would like the complete answer to be entered into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I will be happy to do that. I'm just not following what -- I'm sorry. If Your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Page 41, line 4. "I'm not familiar with the larger document, so I don't know anything more about that." Defence counsel says that was not the complete answer. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic, I asked you about D2/4 and whether it formed part of a larger document or whether it stood by itself, and you said -- you gave an answer. Can you -- to the effect that you were not familiar with the larger document and you don't know anything more about that. Can you just try and now repeat the answer that you gave, your full answer that you gave?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that there was a larger document, and I was not familiar with it at all. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Your Honours, but all of us here who speak B/C/S heard the witness say, "It was on its own," and I think that the Prosecutor could ask the witness whether he said that, rather than giving a fresh answer. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Thank you. That's precisely what I was trying to find out, and I'm grateful to my learned friend for pointing that out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did the document exist on its own? Is that what you're saying? In other words, it wasn't part of a larger document?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was not part of a larger document. I wasn't familiar with it. I would have known. I said I was in the board of the party. It is possible. I still don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know about a larger document. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, it's just past 11.00. I won't be much longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If counsel wishes, we can again ask the audio unit to give us a correct transcript. Yes. It's now 11 hours. We'll have our break and continue at 1130 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution continues re-examination. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: D4/4, please. Would you have a look at that. Now, your position is that you don't know the person who apparently signed the receipt, this Dzananovic Nerfid?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am hearing the name for the first time, and I don't know the document either. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. D5/4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I wonder, just going back to the last document, if I could just clarify with the witness the answer. He said, "I'm hearing the name for the first time, and I don't know the document either." The last part, "I don't know the document either," I'd like a clarification on what he means by that. MR. DI FAZIO: I'll ask, if Your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You heard the Judge's inquiry. When you say you don't know the document, do you mean that you've never seen it before? Are you not familiar with this type of document? Can you amplify upon that so that we understand precisely what you mean when you say, "I don't know the document."

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never seen it until my arrival here to the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. D5/4. Now, this is a document apparently signed by yourself. Do you know, are you able to state clearly, what O/4 and M/160 refers to in that document?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you shed any light on the meaning of the words, "I will use the above-mentioned objects in accordance to the order of the person who gave me the objects, or his representative, and turn the objects back upon his request"?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that I formulated a text of that kind. I don't know who wrote it down like that. I see my signature. How it came to be there, I don't know. Maybe it's a real document. But I'd like to see the original somewhere, and then I could confirm or refute. I don't know, this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: The signature -- you may have been asked this. Forgive me. The signature, is it apparently yours?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging -- to all intents and purposes, yes, 99 per cent it is, although my signatures tend to vary. I don't always sign myself the same way. So I'd like to see the original for that reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. The document itself also has a series of lines drawn in, obviously for someone to fill in that part of the document. Can you tell us if this is some sort of standard-form document, or you can't tell us?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And just a final question on this document. In his questioning, Mr. Pisarevic put this question to you, and you provided this answer:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: This ammunition, this ammunition mentioned here, could you tell us what it means, 0/4 and M/160?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't know that either. It was a long time ago. Now, I just want to be absolutely certain about your position on this reference to 0/4 and M/160.
