Mr. Pisarevic assumed, by virtue of his question, that it was ammunition. Is it still your position that you simply don't know what it's a reference to?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what it's a reference to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now look at D6/4? MR. DI FAZIO: Does the witness have the original? Because the original was also provided into evidence at a later stage. There was a photocopy and an English translation and also the original of this particular document. I think this was given a different exhibit number than D6/4. It may in fact be D7, unless I'm mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The one that we said looks like a carbon copy. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, that's the one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. MR. DI FAZIO: It's clearer. That's the only reason I need it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes, you can see the stamp. It's a bit clearer there and it says, stamp: "Military post Number 2130 Slavonski Brod." Would that indicate that the document was stamped on its way either into or out of Croatia at Slavonski Brod?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say anything about the document because I didn't take part in it. I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You're not familiar with that sort of stamp?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart from what it says, I never encountered a stamp of this kind before.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: I've done with those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I'm now asking you questions again about your evidence in answer to Mr. Pisarevic's questions on the 17th of October. He asked you of -- whether you attended, on behalf of the SDA, a meeting with representatives of the Croatian Democratic Community. You said that there was an attempt, but you managed to break it up and nothing came of it. And then Mr. Pisarevic asked you a further question about a meeting held in Prud on the 19th of May, 1992, that you went there uninvited, expressed your opinion, and that no joint Crisis Staff or anything like that was formed. I'd just like to be clear about this meeting. Who were the participants in it? And by that I don't mean necessarily individuals. I'm more interested in groupings, any parties or official bodies.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exclusively representatives of the HDZ and SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Why did you go uninvited? And if you could also comment on why you didn't get an invitation. Those are two questions, I know, but if you could answer both of those.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's like this: Many people didn't believe me, either side, because of my unfortunate and also beautiful surname, although I -- and I claim today the same thing, that I was -- in all the events that were taking place, I tried to be as honest as possible, as realistic as possible, as frank and open as possible. And I think that I was somebody who could do everything but the kind of things that would lead to the worst. And if I had to speak for a thousand days, I would always be against events taking the turn that they did turn. Tihic and Fitozovic were invited, but I took it upon myself to go. They told me because they knew I would hear of it. And I said, "Well, I'm going with you too to see what they want." And when I arrived I saw what I saw, and I did what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. So invitations were extended to SDA officials but you weren't included in the invitation list.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that they received oral invitations, but nobody received any written invitations, nobody at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You say that nothing came of it and that there was no joint Crisis Staff. Was that an official position adopted by the -- sorry. Was that the result of an official position adopted by the SDA?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What was the basis of your opposition to such a proposition?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the very beginning, from the time that the party was formed and throughout its duration, all the time and even today, I never was a combatant or advocate of the creation of any kind of coalition with one side of the two sides involved. We're either going to be all three of us together, all three sides together, or not at all. That was my position from the very beginning, and that is my position today as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Pisarevic was still questioning you about that meeting, and you stated that you realised where the meeting was leading and that you were -- the SDA was not going to participate in such a meeting, and then you all walked out or you walked out. Then Mr. Pisarevic put to you this question:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the fact that it was decided at that time that the commanders of the joint armed units should be Marko Bozanovic, a Croat, and Mr. Alija Fitozovic, a Muslim? Now, my question is: Were you aware of any joint armed units at all, regardless of who was their head?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no joint units. If some of the Muslims were on the side of the HVO, which was seen in the war, then there were Muslims in the 4th Detachment as well, and we never speak about a coalition of any kind. It was the will of certain individuals who --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, we've heard evidence that Bozanovic and Fitozovic were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. Would we let the witness finish his answer? I mean, throughout these couple of days we have been insisting on giving the opportunity to the witness to finish his answer and now are we changing the rules?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. No, we are not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Sometimes it's just the overlap. So let him complete the answer. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please. MR. DI FAZIO: I didn't realise that I had cut off the witness. I heard a -- I certainly didn't mean to cut him off.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: If I cut you off, Mr. Izetbegovic, I apologise. Please complete your answer.

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it appeared that you cut me off, but I just wanted to add two more words. Otherwise, I answered, to all intents and purposes. If there were any Muslims in the HVO, then there were also some of them on the 4th Detachment side. That is their personal affair. They opted for that themselves. We were not the ones who went to convince people and say, "You're Muslims, you must be here. That's where you ought to be." It was the free will and decision of the citizens. So that's my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Bozanovic and Fitozovic were, we have heard, appointed as commanders or in high-ranking positions in the TO. That appointment or those appointments, I should say, resulted from a meeting. Was it this meeting in Prud or was it another meeting where it was decided that they would become heads of the TO or hold high rank in the TO?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While we were in Prud, there was no mention of the Territorial Defence. That followed the next day, and it was quite different.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Pisarevic asked you this question and you gave this answer, and he was talking about the general instability in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was it because of this uncertainty and insecurity and the general state of affairs as it was that the SDA started to form party patrols which had their checkpoints during the night in the town of Samac itself?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely because of the prevailing situation, one in which there was no security any more. There was no safety for the citizens of the towns, the Muslims saw to that. They had the right to self-organisation to protect themselves. That was the sole purpose and none other. Your answer doesn't make clear your position on the issue of SDA checkpoints. Did the SDA establish checkpoints throughout the town during the night?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the checkpoints did exist, but there was a list for the duty people to be on duty during the night that was sent to the police station in Samac, so that nothing was secret, nothing was clandestine, and some of the work was done together, jointly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What sort of checkpoints were these? Checkpoints where cars were stopped, or something else?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. It was pure observation. Nobody had the right to intervene in any way. They were just there to observe and monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: That's what I mean. The word "checkpoint" imports a certain activity. It imports that people might be stopped, questioned, then allowed to move on. I want to understand if it was that sort of checkpoint, something the police might normally set up on a road, or the army, that sort of thing, or was it something altogether different?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't that type of checkpoint. It was pure observation, and if somebody attempted to do anything, something that was not in keeping with proper conduct, then they could prevent an individual from doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Pisarevic, on Thursday, the 18th, asked you some questions about your movements around the town on the 17th of April. You said in evidence that you drove a red Yugo Kedi - I'm not sure if I've got the car right, but I think it's enough to identify the type of car that you mentioned - and that you drove it home. How do you reconcile that with your evidence that you went to your daughter's apartment to evade capture?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My daughter was at their uncle's, her husband's aunt, in fact. That's where she was. And I went there to leave the car. I took the keys to her flat and went to the flat alone, on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: So you didn't go home -- when you said you went home, you didn't go to your residence; you went to your daughter's residence?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, if I may interrupt, before we rise, we may need ten minutes for some housekeeping matters we need to discuss before Monday. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I can assure you that I don't intend to be more than a few more minutes, and then we'll have our next witness to call.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, precisely that, because we're trying to discuss something before the next witness comes. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. That will be done. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You said, in answer to counsel for Mr. Tadic, Mr. Krgovic, that you participated in some exchanges, three in all, exchanges that occurred in Bosanski Samac. Who was exchanged? Who was being exchanged on these occasions?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prisoners were being exchanged from the battlefront at Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Soldiers?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were very few soldiers. All of them were in civilian clothing. There were elderly people and women, a lot of elderly people and women from Vukovar, sick people, all kinds of people. There were no soldiers from Vukovar at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: So what ethnic background were the people who were being held in Bosanski Samac prior to the exchange? Were they Croats, Serbs, Muslims, or mixtures?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were mostly Serbs and Croats. They were being exchanged, no others. There were perhaps some Muslims here and there, but that was a rarity, somebody who happened to find themselves there at that particular time, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Who were they being exchanged for?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One side would bring their own people in a bus and the other side would do the same, and then they would switch buses. People from one bus would move to the other and vice versa. And us locals were present there to organise this, to give them some sandwiches, something to eat, some first aid, food. And everybody received that assistance, both parties, but the Vukovar people had to stay on - this was done by the Red Cross - until they received agreement and were allowed to -- until Croatia said that it would accept them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam President, we have to clarify, and I think we have to ignore the question, a part of the question of my learned colleague. It's page 52, line 3. He said, "So what ethnic background were the people who were being held in Bosanski Samac?" which my understanding is that these people are maybe in detention or in camp or whatever, and then going to exchanges. But obviously, the witness said, very precisely, they just switched the buses in Samac, who was the transit point or something like that. So if my learned colleague can clarify that, because this formulation, "being held," I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. You want that clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure the Prosecutor got that. MR. DI FAZIO: I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's the use of the word "held" that the counsel is concerned -- MR. DI FAZIO: I'm just looking at the transcript, and may I just very briefly confer with my colleague before I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Right. I think I understand the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: The people who were in Bosanski Samac being exchanged, were they being held, or you can't comment on that? In other words, were they prisoners or not apparently prisoners?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could leave Samac freely, and we even took some people to lunch at the hotel, to have something to eat, until the order came from their side that they could start on their exchange journey and that they would be accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you know how the people came to be in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I sat with a group of them on one occasion in the hotel while they were having lunch. We went to dress some of them, because they were in pajamas. They had been taken out of the hospital. We gave them clothes to wear from the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And do you know how long before April 16 these exchanges took place?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was saying, there were several exchanges, so I can't remember. When an exchange was happening, there were many representatives from Belgrade, from Zagreb, from the military structures of both sides, and we, as the hosts - at least that's how we considered ourselves to be - we helped them as much as we could, as far as the humanitarian side is concerned. We didn't help in any other way. Of course, we helped as much as we could. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. di Fazio. I wonder whether we can go back to your question as to line 53.21, where you say, "Do you know how the people came to be in Bosanski Samac?" And Mr. Izetbegovic's answer is: "I do." And then he talks about sitting with them at lunch, but we don't get an answer beyond the "I do." Could we have a little bit of elaboration, please. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: The people you sat with at lunch, how did they come to be --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How did they come to be in Bosanski Samac? How had they arrived there? How had they been taken there?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were exchanged. This side, the Serb side, went immediately across the bridge in the direction of Belgrade, I suppose. There were cases when from Zagreb approval had not been given to accept them. So we had no other way out but to take them to the hotel to warm up, for some of them to change, and to have something to eat. That's how it was, and that is how it went on. And when approval arrived for them to leave, they left. No one slept.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. You've described -- you told the Court how they left, but how did they get there in the first place? How did they get to Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We took them, because there was no point in keeping them there, to make them suffer even more than they had suffered already. We tried to ease the situation for them, to have something to eat, to refresh themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did they arrive in buses in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The buses came in front of the hotel. They got off the buses, went into the hotel, then from the hotel back to the buses again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Where had the buses come from?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The exchange took place in the customs-free zone in Bosanski Samac, right next to the bridge on the Sava River, and from there to Samac it's about 3 kilometres, and that is why we took them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Those people that you looked after, fed, took to lunch to the hotel, were they people coming into Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean "coming into."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: They were not resident of Bosanski Samac. It looks like they came from somewhere else, from outside the town. Where did they come from? With their buses, where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They came from the direction of Vukovar. They were brought there as prisoners of the Croatian army and Croatian citizens. They came from that part to be exchanged. We took them to Samac. There was no one from Samac. They were all from the Vukovar area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Izetbegovic. Mr. Pisarevic asked you questions about people abandoning the town of Bosanski Samac, and he asked you this:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You mentioned that there was unrest in town, that people were taking their children out of town. Does that mean that the town of Bosanski Samac, in that period of time, was being abandoned by entire families or parts of families? And you replied:

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both, whole families and parts of families. Now, are you -- were you saying there that people were abandoning the town of Bosanski Samac on a permanent basis, going and never coming back again? Is that what you were saying?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What did you mean?

utterances.speaker: IZET IZETBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everyone went thinking that it would last a couple of days and then that it would be over and they would come back. They didn't go far. They went to neighbouring villages, some to Slavonia. Whoever had someone close by, family or friends, they went there where there was no danger.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. You were asked questions by Mr. Pantelic yesterday -- I'll withdraw that question. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we release the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What did you want to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I just want to have a right, with your permission, to a very narrow issue, one question in re-cross in order to clarify something which is in the interest of justice --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- and complete the facts --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- for the information of this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. You don't cross-examine twice. After the examination, that's the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I think it will be very useful for this Trial Chamber to know these two directions, and actually, I want to help to my learned friends from Prosecutor, and as well as the Trial Chamber, in order to establish these very simple facts about the ways of buses coming from one point to Samac and vice versa. I mean that's the only question that I want to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You see, the Trial Chamber doesn't want to establish a precedent where after re-examination counsel for the Defence, and even for the Prosecution when it comes to the Defence case, to do what you're trying to do. What is the point? First state the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. The point is I want to ask a very simple question of Mr. Izetbegovic, from which town the buses came in Samac. There are two towns, two regions actually in Croatia. And who conducted these exchanges, you know, in order to clarify. Because it doesn't seem to me it's clear from the transcript that that was the case. So that's my intention, but, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Why? You have your intention --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: About the principle, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you remain silent when I'm talking to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I've explained the point, and I'm sure the witness has understood what clarification you need. So the Trial Chamber will adopt it and ask the witness to answer and clarify. MR. DI FAZIO: I don't think he's quite understood -- I don't think the witness has quite understood that the Chamber is putting the question to him now rather than --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Did you catch what Mr. Pantelic was saying yourself, Mr. di Fazio? You had your microphone off. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Yes. I heard, yes. Do you want me to ask the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do I need to say anything?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let me ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel for the Defence wanted clarification on the people you said had come from Vukovar. He wanted to find -- on the buses. He wanted to find out in which regions they came from, if you do, or which towns they came from other than Vukovar, or if Vukovar is a region. Can you explain, as far as you know, where they came from, the towns, the regions, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Except by the licence plates of the buses, I can't know anything more. I didn't have lists of names of the people in the buses. My duty was to provide humanitarian aid. There were Zagreb, Vukovar, and Cakovec registration plates and also Vinkovci registration plates. So this side that brought them, who I assume were Serb prisoners, they had licence plates from Zagreb, Vinkovci, Cakovec. As for those from Vukovar, they were Croatian prisoners. I just saw the licence plates, no others than those I have mentioned. I didn't see any others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The examination is through with you, and we are very grateful that you have been very patient and have given evidence to the Tribunal to assist us in our trials. Thank you very much. You are released.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. We do not have any questions or things like that for this witness, but maybe it would be useful, because during the re-examination, the Prosecutor has showed the document D5/4, which was in the copy. We would like to offer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The witness can be led out. Yes, the witness can be led out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And we think it would be useful just to see the original of this document, because the witness stated that he was 90 per cent certain that it is his signature, but maybe he should see this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Where was the original in the proceedings? When he was being examined, where was the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We had it, Your Honours, during, but we did not believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You said that. But why didn't you offer the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Because the witness did not make any doubt about his signature. Now he said it's maybe 90 per cent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Immediately he said that, and you knew you had the original, why didn't you bring it up? Why didn't you do that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We were waiting for the Prosecutor to finish his re-cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. You can't give that as an excuse. You have seen your colleagues intervene, object, do whatever they want to do during the re-examination. Those are things which will not be accepted by the Trial Chamber. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: As Judge May said some time back, these are not trials by ambush. All right? You put your case on the table. The other side puts their case on the table. Okay? No more --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'll leave it with the Prosecution, if they think it's worth pursuing, to deal with it. Yes, Ms. Baen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have any problems or anything other than a question, because I'm not familiar exactly with how this works over here. Is this witness being released now? Is he going to talk to the Victims and Witnesses people now for the investigation or is he going to be coming back and do we get a report? I'm just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: The investigation with Mr. Izetbegovic, about his conversation or what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You have no confidence when the Trial Chamber says the matter is under investigation?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: No, I have total confidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So what is your problem?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: My question is: Is he leaving now or is he going to talk to them now or is he coming back and do we get a report? I just don't know. It's a different procedure than from where I come from so that's why I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So you just wait. If all you wanted to do was remind the Chamber about it, you should have done so. So you don't ask about the procedures.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'm just asking for the state of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The matter will be taken care of.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: We will receive a report? That's all I'm asking. I don't understand. I've read all the jurisprudence here in the ICTY, and I haven't seen this procedure before, so I'm just asking if we get a report, because all my co-counsels are asking me how it's done in the United States. It's done differently. So I'm merely asking, very respectfully, Your Honour, if we're going to receive a report as to what the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will take a decision, and the Trial Chamber will inform the parties.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution -- I wanted to find out who the next witness is. MR. DI FAZIO: The next witness is Hasan Bicic and that witness will be led through his evidence by my colleague Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. I just wanted to raise the issue that was discussed at pre-trial stage regarding conflict of interests concerning Mr. Pisarevic and his client Mr. Simo Zaric. I'm sure you've read the pre-trial proceedings. MR. DI FAZIO: I have read them. I haven't read them recently. This --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because the Trial Chamber has been reminded of the issues that were raised then. We just want to be sure that now that the trial is proceeding whether the matters were as they were discussed and decided, and I would like to hear from Mr. Pisarevic, who is counsel for Mr. Simo Zaric, again. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, perhaps before we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That matter is discussed, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: No, no. Before you call upon the Defence, I'm informed by my -- by Mr. Weiner that the two witnesses who are to be called, the Bicic brothers, were in fact represented in legal proceedings or some legal matter - I don't know the nature of it - in Yugoslavia by Mr. Pisarevic. Now, problems that might arise, I don't know, but I just thought I would inform the Chamber that that is the fact, that is the situation, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: From the point of view of the Prosecution, you have no problem with Mr. Pisarevic cross-examining these witnesses? MR. DI FAZIO: May I just confer with my colleagues briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because we want to discuss that fully so that it doesn't arise in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Obviously, the Prosecution is concerned that because of the previous relationship on our case that existed between Mr. Pisarevic and the Bicic brothers, there may well be some prejudice caused to the Prosecution by the fact that Mr. Pisarevic has access to all sorts of what normally would be privileged, I suppose, information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Were the proceedings on similar events? MR. DI FAZIO: No. No, no. They're some sort of civil matter, I understand -- business, some sort of business matter, Mr. Weiner tells me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just be clear. These two witnesses are not the ones who have allegations against some of the accused persons where Mr. Pisarevic was allegedly present? MR. DI FAZIO: No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: They are not the ones? MR. DI FAZIO: No. No. No. No. No. I see. Mr. Pisarevic arises very briefly in the evidential scenario that these witnesses will describe during the time of their incarceration, but not in a manner that should cause the Prosecution any concern. And before I finally make my position on that, may I just briefly confer with my colleagues, who have been proofing these two witnesses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- and who have more -- who have a clearer idea about the significance of this encounter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And while the Prosecution is doing that, I would like Mr. Pisarevic to think about what was raised at the pre-trial stage, and also Mr. Simo Zaric, because I'll come to you two later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I'm grateful for that indulgence. The situation is this: Mr. Pisarevic, I understand, has recently represented these two gentlemen, these two Bicic brothers, in proceedings to obtain the return of a home or land or something in the former Yugoslavia. That's one aspect. As far as the evidential scenario of events in 1992 are concerned, there will be evidence from these witnesses that they spoke or attempted to speak with Mr. Pisarevic on the day of the takeover, what the Prosecution says is the takeover. There will also be evidence from one of them, one of the Bicic brothers, that they were temporarily released, following a beating, and taken to their homes and at one stage encountered Mr. Pisarevic outside of a pizza bar, a pizza bar I think that they owned themselves. That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: These are the two. Are there any others on the list who appear to be concerned with -- MR. DI FAZIO: Any other witnesses?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, who may be concerned with Mr. -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, there are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Who may be alleging that Mr. Pisarevic was present when certain incidents were happening to them? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Yes. I understand. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: I can't give you an exhaustive list as I stand here. However, I can tell you that one of the witnesses who apparently speaks of contact with Mr. Pisarevic during events (redacted) (redacted), and I know that other witnesses talk about Mr. Pisarevic from time to time in their statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Let's do it this way: Since the immediate one and the following one you think are not going to make the allegations like Mr. Pisarevic was there but they were represented by Mr. Pisarevic, so that is not the point. These are the witnesses. So if you provide the list of these witnesses whom, according to your case, make allegations that when certain incidents, which are the basis of some of these crimes, were happening, Mr. Pisarevic was there, in a situation where it would mean that Mr. Pisarevic may be a witness, all right? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So when you have that list, give it to the Defence, the whole team, and also make sure that -- okay. It's up to the Defence counsels, really, to make sure that their clients get these names. So that we know exactly when to ask co-counsel to cross-examine, to avoid the conflict of interest and also to avoid possible intimidation by the witnesses -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- on their own. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because they may be intimidated by the mere fact that -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- this is the counsel who -- MR. DI FAZIO: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- was present at the time these incidents were happening, not that Mr. Pisarevic will be intimidating them, but just the presence -- MR. DI FAZIO: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- yes, can affect the witnesses. And I want Mr. Simo Zaric to understand these things, what I'm saying, correctly so that when the time comes, we can deal with this matter. Because, as the Trial Chamber, we have the duty to see to it that the trial is fair, is dignified, the witnesses are not unduly intimidated, they are free to give evidence as much as -- of the things that they know about, so that the presence of anybody in the courtroom should not be used as having had an undue influence on them, in which case, the accused in question who has that particular counsel may raise the issue on appeal and apply to the Appeal Chamber that the proceedings were not fair because he didn't -- he does not think then that his counsel fully represented him because of the possible conflict of interest. Because these things may not actually happen, but the perception is important. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And it is the duty of the Trial Chamber to see to it that that is avoided; if necessary, ask a co-counsel to do the cross-examination. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Well, I understand that, and I, with respect, entirely agree. The Prosecution will seek to guard against that eventuality happening. We'll conduct a search of the statements, we'll revise them, we will see where Mr. Pisarevic is mentioned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Appears to be -- MR. DI FAZIO: -- in the statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: And we will provide a report to the Defence and, if necessary, to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, to the Chamber as well. MR. DI FAZIO: And we will also, in addition, when witnesses arrive here and we proof them prior to their giving evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- will be on guard and alive to that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: So with respect, it's a good idea. It will be done, and we'll cover those concerns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. So the next witness we okay. Mr. Pisarevic can cross-examine. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because there's no allegation that he was present. MR. DI FAZIO: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. MR. DI FAZIO: Other than --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Other than having -- MR. DI FAZIO: Other than being --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Represented. MR. DI FAZIO: -- outside the pizza hut, pizza establishment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- on an occasion when one of the Bicic brothers was released temporarily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: And a couple of -- yes, and a couple of telephone calls on the day of the takeover.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Yes. So we can proceed. You can call the witness. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. May I just say one more thing on that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: We have nothing to cause us any concern on the instructions that we -- or the instructions that we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You have -- MR. DI FAZIO: -- found on the telephone calls. Now, I'm speaking from the Prosecution's point of view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: The Defence know something that they -- or allege that something happened during those telephone calls in particular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What's -- the telephone calls since they came into the -- MR. DI FAZIO: On the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- we started the trial, or when? MR. DI FAZIO: No, no. This is on the day of the takeover, back in 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, okay. On the events in 1992. MR. DI FAZIO: The instructions we've taken on that don't cause us, at this stage, any alarm. However, I can't speak for the Defence. They may have all sorts of different versions of those phone calls, and it's up to them to exercise their judgement and decide whether or not their own instructions are such that will bring Mr. Pisarevic into some sort of conflict --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- where he might be called upon to testify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- or placed in that position. I can't speak for them. That's their problem. But as far as the Prosecution is concerned, and on the material that we have, we're not alarmed about that at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Yes. Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. If I may, Madam President. According to our well-established practice, prior to the witness will be brought in, we have to change the positions of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see. MR. DI FAZIO: Mr. Milan Simic, just a few of them, just a matter of principle, nothing more. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll deal with that. I want Mr. Pisarevic to be on inquiry that at one stage he will be called upon to deal with the issues that have been discussed, and it may be necessary that his co-counsel cross-examines the witness. I want you to understand clearly that the Trial Chamber is not alleging that you are likely to conduct yourself improperly; it is the perception, and also the protection of the Prosecution witnesses. So when we reach that stage, we may have to ask co-counsel to cross-examine those particular witnesses, all right? And I want Mr. Simo Zaric to understand that so you can deal with that off the Bench, when we come into Court, just before we deal with those witnesses concerning these issues we have raised, we are all clear as to what is happening, and also your co-counsel can be prepared if he is called upon. And I want to make it clear that it is not according -- you know, it won't be according to your decision; it will be the Trial Chamber's decision. So maybe we can carry out the swap, asked by the Defence, as long as the security officers are not interfered with.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam President, if I may, just a second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do we have ten minutes prior to one hour to discuss some procedural evidential issues or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Regarding this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No. Regarding the other previous issues that we raised several weeks ago, I mean videotapes, audiotapes, stuff like that. I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. In fact, I was just reminded by the legal officer about that. About the requests on videotapes, the Trial Chamber has looked into the matter and has found out that the correct procedure is for the Defence counsel to ask for these videotapes from the Registrar, in writing, putting across their reasons. Because this is not the normal procedure, but if you put down your reasons why you are seeking these videotapes for your use in the Defence case, then it will be up to the Registrar to respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Madam President. And also, I would like to ask for your assistance with regard to the audiotapes, because, as you well know, we have some problems, you know, with the exact words in B/C/S language what was said or not of the witnesses. So we would like to have, if it's possible, let's say one or two days after the testimony, this copy of audiotape, so that we can check by ourselves, and then in writing, in writing form, to inform the Trial Chamber or the Registry about the annotations, you know, and stuff like that, you know. Because you -- in some cases you cannot hear what the witness said in his own native language, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. What you do is you make separate applications.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: For the videotapes, a separate one, because the reasons will be different; for the audiotapes, also a separate one, so that the Registrar has these things on record. It is much easier to catch anything once it's on record.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, if you can do that, because you are asking that you need the audiotapes every two days, so you deal with that in writing so that we have a record.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Madam President. And also, about the issue of Mr. Donia's report in other case, which was under seal, we obtained, according to the order of -- on Judge Rodrigues's Trial Chamber, actually, he granted our request, subject to agreement between our Defence teams and Defence team in that case, Prijedor case. So we filed that yesterday, and actually, we completed everything, so we are waiting for the development about that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What did you file yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We filed an agreement which was according to the directions in Judge Rodrigues's decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We filed an agreement between our Defence in our case and the Defence in their case, in Mladjo Radic case, before Judge Rodrigues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So now we are at that stage and we would like to know when this report can be handed to us, and then we shall decide whether to proceed with the other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. Okay. Yes. The Trial Chamber will deal with that as soon as we see copies of what you filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So possibly on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So the next witness can come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please make your solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could the witness please state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: My name is Hasan Bicic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: I was born in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: On the 11th of June, 1960.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Do you have -- did you have family at the time in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could you tell us who the family were, brothers, sisters, your mother, your father?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: It was my brother and his wife and daughter my mother.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Had your family lived in Bosanski Samac for a long time?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was born there. My father was also originally from Samac, that is to say, my family is one of several families which formed Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So is it accurate to say that generations of Bicics have lived in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Well, you could say from the founding of the town itself, that my father's family on my father's side, the family lived in Samac, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Where do you live now?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: I now live in Germany for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: In April 1992, where were you living?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: In Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you attend primary school in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, are you -- I'm going to ask you about some of the defendants in this case to which you're testifying. Are you familiar with Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Have you known Milan Simic a long time?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you attend primary school with Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Do you know Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you attend primary school with Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Would you be able to indicate to the Trial Chamber today whether you see Milan Simic and Blagoje Simic in this room?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: For the record, could you please indicate who you believe to be Milan Simic and then after that who you -- where in this room you believe Blagoje Simic to be sitting?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Yes. Milan Simic is to the left in a wheelchair. Blagoje Simic is the third, moving from left to right, with a beard.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Can I just have the record reflect that both Milan Simic and Blagoje Simic have been correctly identified by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, are you aware whether Mr. Blagoje Simic and Mr. Milan Simic are related in any way?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Do you know the relationship between them?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: I think they're cousins.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. After you did primary school in Bosanski Samac, did you remain in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: No. After primary school, I went to Sarajevo to attend secondary school there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And after secondary school?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: After secondary school I came back to Samac where I took over the family restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What is the nature of that restaurant?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: How do you mean what is the nature of the restaurant was?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was it -- basically was -- was your restaurant a pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: No. It was a family restaurant where we served a la carte food, a la carte menus. And later on I opened a pizza bar.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I take it that you have more than one family business interest in Bosanski Samac then?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Yes, later on. After the restaurant, that is. We had several other catering establishments in town.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: In this latter period, was one of those catering establishments a pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just wish to show the defendant [sic] what's on the record as Exhibit P9. This is the map which has been subject to various markings by previous witnesses, and I -- we have clean copies of that map, and depending on what the Trial Chamber thinks is the most appropriate way to proceed, I would propose to give a clean copy to the witness and have it marked as P9B and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I just want to make sure that the clean copies have also been given to the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: No. We just have -- well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let me just ask the usher --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I didn't expect it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Let me ask the usher to show it so we know it is the exact copy of P9.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Sometimes there can be -- yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Probably it is a mistake in 76 page, line 8. Our learned colleague just mentioned "defendant." Probably she thought the "witness."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I just wish to show "defendant." So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Just to make sure that it's the replica of P9, because we don't want one and the same copy to be marked by so many witnesses, otherwise it will cause confusion when writing the judgement or indeed on appeal, if the case goes to appeal. Can we get the number? We would be grateful if it would be P9 something.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit P9D.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: May I also ask the usher to give the witness a pen or -- if he has one.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, I think you can see in front of you a town plan of Bosanski Samac. I'd ask you to indicate on it as best you can where your pizzeria was and also where your home was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can he do it with numbers, like 1, 2?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So less confusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, can you mark on the map with a number 1 where your house was.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: I've marked it, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: May I suggest to -- may I just use a smaller pen?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: As far as I'm able to find my way on the map. I've done it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now please mark on the same map with a number 2 where you recall your pizzeria being located.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: At this stage I don't intend to ask the defendant -- the witness to mark anything else on the map, but if it could be remained -- if it could remain with the witness so that we can cross-refer to it should it be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That's all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, this pizzeria which you've marked on the map, was it a successful business?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Fairly successful, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And -- so that I take it you had many clientele?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Well, I had many, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What sort of people would come to your restaurant?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Could you clarify that? You mean ethnically speaking or social strata? What do you mean by the sort of people?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'll limit it at this stage just to whether people of all ethnic groups living in Bosanski Samac used to frequent your pizzeria.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Absolutely so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: May I ask whether any of the defendants in this case used to frequent your pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: For the record, could you state whether -- which of the defendants used to frequent your pizzeria or whether all of them did?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Of those present here, I think the one who was our most frequent guest was Milan Simic. And from time to time, I think that Miroslav Tadic and Mr. Zaric would come by. Blagoje Simic wasn't in the establishment even once ever, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You've mentioned that Miroslav Tadic used to come by. Did you have other contact with Miroslav Tadic apart from when he was a guest or a client in your restaurant?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: He wasn't a frequent guest, but he would drop by from time to time. But we did have contacts. That is to say, we were members of an organisation. It was called the Presidency of the Association for Craftsmen of our municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, if I could ask you whether the witness should be identifying that Mr. Tadic and Mr. Simic are actually present in the room here as you did with Mr. Milan Simic and Mr. Blagoje Simic, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, absolutely. I was just coming to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, you've heard Judge Williams' directions. Can you please identify whether you see Mr. Miroslav Tadic in this room and if so, where he is?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: I can see him, and he is second in order from left to right.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Just to clarify, is that on the back row against the wall?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I think the record can show that Mr. Miroslav Tadic is being correctly identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And finally, you said that occasionally Simo Zaric came to your restaurant. Similarly, could you identify to the Chamber if he's in the room, and if so, where he's located?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: I also said that Mr. Zaric did come by but not frequently, and he's sitting up in front.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I think the record can also reflect that Mr. Simo Zaric has been correctly identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, I'd like to take you now just to the few months directly before April 1992, and I would like to ask you some questions about what your knowledge is of the events in Samac at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: At this stage could I ask for the Exhibit P14A, which I believe is the clear copy or the unmarked copy of the photographs to be presented to the witness. I don't know whether it's necessary for the -- well, my next question is not directly related to a photograph, but in this line of questioning I will be referring to the exhibit. I don't know whether the usher --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What you do, if you just direct the usher, "Can you prepare photograph number so-and-so, number so-and-so, number so-and-so," so that he can be putting them to the ELMO as your questions come.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: If the usher could prepare photograph number 33.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, can you tell me, in the months -- so we're talking about February, March 1992. Would it be correct to say that there was an increase in tensions in and around Bosnia Samac? And I mean ethnic tensions or political tensions.

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Yes, you could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Is it the case that there were checkpoints and barricades to be found in various locations in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I ask the witness to look at what is now P1A/33, which I believe is on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the scene or the area depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Not from this angle of vision, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Are you saying that you don't know -- you don't know where that place is?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: From this angle, I couldn't say, but let me try. I think it could be Crkvina Street. Crkvina, in fact, is a village some 5 kilometres away from Samac in the direction of Gradacac and Modrica. I think I recognise a detail here, that it is a kiosk, a police checkpoint or something like that. I think that's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to whether there was a checkpoint in and around the road in Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was. I know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Can I ask you who was in charge of that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Uniform -- people in uniform, wearing the uniform of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you yourself ever stopped at that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Can you tell me, when you were stopped, what took place?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Well, I was driving in the direction of Modrica when a group of soldiers stopped me right there. Now I'm sure it was at this junction here. And they told me to get out of the car. They searched the car, and I had to lean up against the car and they frisked me. They searched me in detail, probably looking for something, probably weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to believe that members of the 4th Detachment may have been involved in manning the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Perhaps there's no reason for me to believe that they manned [Realtime transcript read in error "not"] the checkpoint, but there is reason for me to believe that I was searched following orders given by someone from the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what is that reason?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps a week after the search and my car being stopped and me in it, I received a piece of information from a young man, a Serb from Crkvina, who at that particular moment or a little before they stopped me was in a catering enterprise there which is located between Samac and Crkvina, and the bar is Trile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before we proceed, Mr. Zecevic, there was --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. There's a certain problem with the transcript. The question was -- it's at line -- it's at page 81, line 25.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to believe that the members of the 4th Detachment may have been involved in manning the checkpoint? And:

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Perhaps there is no reason for me to believe that there may not the checkpoint. Probably -- because the witness said they were -- "I have no reason to believe that they were manning the checkpoint." Just that is the objection. Thank you. Maybe my learned colleague can again put the question to the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure the Prosecution have picked the point raised by Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And I heard also in translation what Mr. Zecevic said, it's just it didn't appear in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, this is just a technical issue with the transcript. Could I ask you, do you think that the -- or do you have reason to believe that the 4th Detachment were manning the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: I have reason to believe that it was connected to the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: But if --

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: That there was a connection with the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: But is it also correct that previously you did say that you have no reason to believe they might have actually been manning it, but that then you were searched and stopped on directions of a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASAN BICIC
utterances.text: Following orders or information which was given from that where this young man was present, and he told me seven days later that some people told them to stop me and search me, that they got in touch with them somehow and told them to stop and search me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I think that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, our time is -- our clock says 1.00. We will adjourn, and we will resume on Monday at 0930 hours. Next week the schedules may continue in the afternoon if the facilities will be provided. I'm sure the legal officer did inform counsel on both sides. If the facilities we asked for will be provided, then we will have afternoon sessions as well. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours. Do we have any idea when we'll know? Will we know that on Monday or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: On Monday, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because the arrangements, we have been informed, have been made. But whether or not they will actually take place, they will actually be there, we're not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, concerning this arrangement for the facilities, I assume there is facilities for my client Milan Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, at the beginning of the trial, we were told that we will be able to inspect this facilities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And we actually went over there but we inspected actually the room only at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. This is why I was saying we may, because I know that is subject to your looking at the facilities and finding -- yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you understand, of course, our position that after all we are not the ones who practically decide, but we have to consult the medical specialist, the doctor as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because the medical report which was -- which suggested this bed arrangement is clear, and it was given to the people responsible for making these arrangements so that we -- at least in our minds, it's not an ordinary bed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So that's why I'm saying we may continue in the afternoon if the facilities will be available.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That means if they will be available and if they are properly available. Let me put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because as much as we are concerned, the Prosecutor is really not a persecutor. Thank you. We'll adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
